section: International climate initiatives - UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, CDM, Paris Agreement, key COP outcomes, IPCC assessment reports
subsections: Other climate initiatives - founder or type
IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the European Green Deal?
o: A voluntary forest declaration adopted at the 2014 UN Climate Summit
A UNFCCC mechanism for financing adaptation in least developed countries
A plan of the European Union to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, with Farm to Fork as a component
A scientific assessment programme jointly run by WMO and UNEP
accepted.x: The European Green Deal is an EU plan for net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. The Farm to Fork strategy is one of its components.
accepted.tq: Use the exact objective and institutional identity to distinguish the initiative from nearby climate mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding The Climate Group:
1. It is an international non-profit organisation based in London.
2. It was established in 2003.
3. It runs the RE100 and EV100 initiatives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Climate Group is an international non-profit organisation based in London, established in 2003, and it runs RE100 and EV100.
accepted.tq: Check all three linked identity, year and associated initiatives before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Climate Action Tracker is best described as an initiative involving which of the following?
o: The IPCC and the World Meteorological Organization
Climate Analytics and the NewClimate Institute
accepted.x: Climate Action Tracker is an independent scientific analysis initiative of Climate Analytics and the NewClimate Institute.
accepted.tq: Apply the founder-versus-function distinction to avoid confusing it with intergovernmental bodies.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at which event and by which countries?
o: The Rio Earth Summit; India and Brazil
accepted.x: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at COP27 by Spain and Senegal.
accepted.tq: Match the initiative with its launch forum and founding countries.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal aim of the Early Warnings for All initiative, commonly abbreviated as EW4All, is to provide universal early-warning coverage by:
accepted.x: EW4All aims to achieve universal early-warning coverage by 2027.
accepted.tq: Use the year-specific numerical recall pattern and compare the closely spaced distractor years.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Climate Neutral Now is correct?
o: It is an EU programme launched under the Farm to Fork strategy.
It is a voluntary initiative of the UNFCCC secretariat launched in 2015.
It is a scientific assessment body established by WMO and UNEP.
It is a compulsory mechanism created by the Kyoto Protocol in 1997.
accepted.x: Climate Neutral Now is a voluntary initiative of the UNFCCC secretariat, launched in 2015.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct body, year and voluntary nature while rejecting swapped institutional descriptions.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC):
1. It was launched in 2012.
2. UNEP and six countries were involved in its launch.
3. It targets short-lived climate pollutants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The CCAC was launched in 2012 by UNEP and six countries, and it targets short-lived climate pollutants.
accepted.tq: Verify the date, founding participants and target area as three independent statement components.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The New York Declaration on Forests is associated with which of the following pairs?
o: 2007 Bali Conference and phase-out of ozone-depleting substances
1992 Rio Summit and compulsory finance by OECD countries
2014 UN Climate Summit and voluntary, non-binding action to halt deforestation
accepted.x: The New York Declaration on Forests was endorsed at the 2014 UN Climate Summit and is voluntary and non-binding, with the objective of halting deforestation. It also formed the basis of the Bonn Challenge target of 350 Mha.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the declaration by its year, voluntary character and forest objective.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Bonn Challenge target associated with the New York Declaration on Forests is restoration of:
accepted.x: The New York Declaration on Forests provided the basis for the Bonn Challenge target of restoring 350 million hectares.
accepted.tq: Test the exact quantitative target rather than the broader forest objective.
accepted.sec: Other climate initiatives - founder or type  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):
1. It was adopted on 9 May 1992.
2. It was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit.
3. It entered into force on 21 March 1994.
4. Its secretariat is located in Bonn, Germany.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992, opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit, entered into force on 21 March 1994, and has its secretariat in Bonn, Germany.
accepted.tq: Separate adoption, signature, entry into force and headquarters facts instead of treating them as one date.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992 at:
o: Kyoto, before being opened for signature at Paris
Bonn, before being opened for signature at New York
Rio de Janeiro, before being opened for signature at Kyoto
New York, before being opened for signature at Rio
accepted.x: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992 in New York and was subsequently opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the place of adoption from the place where the treaty was opened for signature.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The UNFCCC seeks primarily to:
o: Stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level preventing dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system
Provide only financial assistance to small island developing States
Regulate international trade in endangered species
Eliminate all industrial production in developed countries
accepted.x: The objective of the UNFCCC is to stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level that prevents dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.
accepted.tq: Select the option stating the treaty’s precise objective rather than one of its related measures.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the UNFCCC, consider the following statements:
1. It has 198 Parties.
2. The Conference of the Parties is its supreme body.
3. The COP ordinarily meets every year.
4. The SBI and SBSTA meet mid-year in Bonn.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The UNFCCC has 198 Parties; the COP is its supreme body and meets annually, while the SBI and SBSTA meet mid-year in Bonn.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional composition, hierarchy and meeting frequency in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the UNFCCC group with its principal obligation?
o: Annex I — provide finance and technology only
Annex II — provide finance and technology to developing countries
Non-Annex I — undertake binding emission cuts identical to Annex I countries
Annex I — receive finance from developing countries
accepted.x: Annex II consists of OECD members of Annex I and is required to provide finance and technology to developing countries. Annex I parties are expected to lead emission cuts, while Non-Annex I parties include developing countries such as India.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure obligation and reject reversed authority or membership claims.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India is classified under which UNFCCC grouping?
o: Annex I and Annex II simultaneously
accepted.x: India is a developing country included among the Non-Annex I Parties. Non-Annex I Parties do not have binding emission cuts under the stated framework and receive special consideration where applicable.
accepted.tq: Use membership discrimination to separate Annex I, Annex II and Non-Annex I categories.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) rests on the idea that:
o: Only developing countries must reduce emissions
All countries have identical historical responsibility and capabilities
Developed countries, having contributed most to historical emissions, should take the lead
Least developed countries must finance mitigation in OECD countries
accepted.x: CBDR-RC recognises differentiated historical responsibility and capabilities; developed countries that caused most historical emissions are expected to take the lead.
accepted.tq: Translate the principle into a practical responsibility allocation rather than memorising only its expansion.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Special consideration under the UNFCCC is specifically associated with which of the following groups?
o: Annex II countries and G7 members only
OECD members and economies in transition only
accepted.x: The UNFCCC gives special consideration to Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and Small Island Developing States (SIDS).
accepted.tq: Decode the paired abbreviations and distinguish vulnerable groups from developed-country categories.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Rio Declaration — Principle 7
2. UNFCCC — Article 3.1
3. Paris Agreement — Article 2.2
4. Kyoto Protocol — Article 10.5
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: CBDR-RC is reflected in Principle 7 of the Rio Declaration, Article 3.1 of the UNFCCC and Article 2.2 of the Paris Agreement. The stated Kyoto Protocol reference is not part of the listed correspondence.
accepted.tq: Use article-number precision to eliminate the swapped or unsupported treaty reference.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The two instruments adopted under the UNFCCC framework are:
accepted.x: The Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement are the two instruments associated with the UNFCCC; their governing meetings are referred to as CMP and CMA respectively.
accepted.tq: Identify the two related instruments while rejecting treaties from other environmental regimes.
accepted.sec: UNFCCC - adoption, Annex parties, CBDR-RC  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was established in 1988 by:
o: UNESCO and the International Union for Conservation of Nature
UNDP and the International Energy Agency
UNEP and the World Meteorological Organization
accepted.x: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
accepted.tq: Apply the institution-founder trap by distinguishing the IPCC’s founding bodies from other environmental organisations.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IPCC:
1. It has 195 member countries.
2. It conducts original research independently of published literature.
3. Its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive.
4. It shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The IPCC has 195 member countries, its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive, and it shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore. It does not conduct its own original research; it assesses published literature.
accepted.tq: Find the single false statement among institutional role and recognition facts.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s: The secretariat of the IPCC is located in:
accepted.x: The IPCC secretariat is located in Geneva.
accepted.tq: Use location discrimination to distinguish the IPCC secretariat from the UNFCCC secretariat in Bonn.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches an IPCC Working Group with its subject?
o: WG III — impacts, adaptation and vulnerability
accepted.x: WG I covers the physical science basis, WG II covers impacts, adaptation and vulnerability, and WG III covers mitigation.
accepted.tq: Use the standard three-way subject mapping and reject the reversed working-group labels.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s: In addition to its three Working Groups, the IPCC has a Task Force on:
accepted.x: The IPCC has a Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official function rather than selecting a broadly related climate activity.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following IPCC Assessment Reports in chronological order:
A. AR4
B. AR1
C. AR5
D. AR2
accepted.x: AR1 was published in 1990, AR2 in 1995, AR4 in 2007 and AR5 in 2014. Therefore, the order is B, D, A, C.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest assessment years, then place the middle reports.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s: The first IPCC Assessment Report, published in 1990, contributed to the development of the:
accepted.x: The IPCC’s First Assessment Report (AR1), published in 1990, fed into the UNFCCC, which was adopted in 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit process.
accepted.tq: Connect the report to its immediate institutional outcome rather than to later climate agreements.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the release date of an AR6 Working Group report?
accepted.x: The AR6 WG I report was released on 9 August 2021. WG II was released on 28 February 2022, WG III on 4 April 2022, and the Synthesis Report on 20 March 2023.
accepted.tq: Discriminate closely spaced dates by matching each date to the correct report component.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report:
1. WG I was released on 9 August 2021.
2. WG II was released on 28 February 2022.
3. WG III was released on 4 April 2022.
4. The Synthesis Report was released on 20 March 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly give the release dates of the AR6 Working Group reports and the Synthesis Report.
accepted.tq: Check a complete date series systematically rather than relying on the year alone.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Seventh Assessment Report (AR7) of the IPCC began in:
accepted.x: The IPCC’s AR7 cycle began in July 2023.
accepted.tq: Test the cycle-start year separately from the projected publication years.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to AR7 of the IPCC, consider the following statements:
1. The Working Group reports are expected around mid-2028.
2. The Synthesis Report is expected by late 2029.
3. The AR7 cycle began in July 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: AR7 began in July 2023; its Working Group reports are due around mid-2028 and its Synthesis Report by late 2029.
accepted.tq: Combine a start date with projected milestones and check each temporal statement independently.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the role of an IPCC Summary for Policymakers (SPM)?
o: It is the annual negotiating text adopted by the UNFCCC COP.
It is a legally binding emission-reduction schedule for Annex I Parties.
It accompanies each assessment report and summarises its findings for policymakers.
It presents the IPCC’s independent original laboratory research only.
accepted.x: Each IPCC assessment report carries a Summary for Policymakers, which presents the assessment findings in a form relevant to policymakers. It is not a legally binding negotiating instrument.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an assessment communication product from a treaty, negotiating text or original research report.
accepted.sec: IPCC - founding bodies, AR1-AR6, working groups, AR7  [other exams]
